articles.title: 15 lakh saplings planted in Bengaluru: BDA now plans website to track their upkeep
articles.description: After questions over the condition of the 15 lakh saplings planted in June, BDA has invited a short-term tender to create a public website showing their maintenance status and progress. The Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) has now moved to create a dedicated website to track the maintenance and progress of the 15 lakh native saplings planted across Bengaluru on June 27. The move comes after questions were raised about the condition and upkeep of the saplings planted during the mass plantation drive held on the occasion of Kempegowda Jayanti. The BDA has issued a short-term tender for developing a post-event platform website through which the public can follow the status of the plantation programme. The plantation drive covered Banashankari, Dr Shivaram Karanth Layout and Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layouts, with a target of planting a total of 1.5 million native saplings. Also Read: Bengaluru beats property giants on rental returns, emerges as India’s top rental-yield market According to the tender notification dated August 6, 2026, the proposed website is intended to bring greater transparency to the maintenance of the saplings and keep the public informed about their condition and progress. The BDA has specifically sought a platform that can provide accurate and real-time information on the maintenance initiative. To ensure transparency in the maintenance of the 1.5 million native saplings planted under BDA's plantation drive on 27 June 2026, and to provide the public with accurate, real-time information on the status of the maintenance initiative, the BDA has invited short-term tenders... pic.twitter.com/FI0nrVN9Ll — Bangalore Development Authority (@BDAOfficialGok) August 6, 2026 The portal will also have a community engagement and contribution system. Through this platform, institutions will be able to adopt plantation sites, while volunteers can participate in weekly activities. Organisations and members of the public will also be able to contribute native saplings, seeds and compost. The proposed system will further allow people to mark special occasions by planting saplings and book educational tours connected to the plantation sites. A separate dashboard is also planned for the programme. It will provide specific login access to BDA officials and NGOs that have adopted plantation sites, allowing them to monitor and update activities related to the sites. Also Read: BMTC online ticketing trouble: QR scanner server down leaves passengers, conductors struggling The BDA had earlier provided an update on the plantation programme on July 27, nearly a month after the drive. It said a review had found that 90% of the saplings and plantation sites were thriving. At that time, the Authority said 279 sites were thriving, while 27 sites were distressed. All the saplings have been geotagged as part of the process for a Guinness World Record. The plantation sites have also been adopted by NGOs and other institutions, which are expected to take responsibility for their maintenance for three years. The latest tender is specifically for the design and development of the post-event website to showcase the progress of this initiative and make information accessible to the public. The tender process began on August 6. The last date for submitting objections regarding the tender is August 12 at 3 pm, while bids can be submitted until August 14 at 3 pm. The technical bids will be opened on August 17 at 3.10 pm, followed by the opening of financial bids after scrutiny of the technical bids. Also Read: BMTC online ticketing trouble: QR scanner server down leaves passengers, conductors struggling If the tender process does not take place on the scheduled date or no bid is received, the deadline for the second call has been fixed as August 21 at 3 pm. The technical bids under the second call will be opened on August 24 at 3.10 pm, with financial bids to be opened after scrutiny of the technical bids. The BDA has stated that a separate tender notice will not be published for the second call. The tender has been issued under Tender Indent No. BDA/2026-27/OW/WORK_INDENT264. Experienced and eligible service firms can access the tender details through the Karnataka government’s e-procurement portal. For further details, firms have been asked to contact the Deputy Conservator of Forests, Bangalore Development Authority, during office hours. The notification also provides the helpline/WhatsApp number 9483166622 and the BDA’s official X handle @BDAOfficialGok for communication. The proposed website is therefore expected to become a public-facing platform for tracking the condition of the 15 lakh saplings, monitoring their maintenance and allowing institutions, NGOs, volunteers and citizens to take part in the plantation programme.

articles.title: MLA KN Singh Deo writes to Odisha CM seeking independent probe into Chattamakhana Dam damage
articles.description: Bhubaneswar: Balangir MLA Kalikesh Narayan Singh Deo has urged Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi to order an urgent and independent technical inquiry into alleged structural damage and design deficiencies in the newly constructed Chattamakhana Dam in Balangir district. In a letter, Singh Deo said the dam's cut-off wall was washed away, and downstream embankments were damaged during recent rains. He described the damage to a recently completed public asset as a serious concern and sought a time-bound investigation into the design, construction and approval process. According to the letter, the project was executed on an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) basis. The MLA alleged that the contractor's sanctioned design differed substantially from the estimated design prepared at the tender stage. The overall length was reduced from 256 metres to 206 metres, while the number of gates came down from 18 to 14. The impervious floor length was also reduced from 80 metres to 50 metres. At the same time, solid retaining walls of 24 metres were added on each flank, which, according to the letter, reduced the clear waterway available for discharge. The estimated project cost was also reduced from around Rs 154 crore to Rs 116 crore. However, the design discharge remained unchanged at 2,760 cubic metres per second (cumec). Singh Deo has questioned whether the reduced waterway can safely handle the retained design discharge. He argued that the shorter impervious floor could affect energy dissipation and seepage control, potentially increasing the risk of downstream scour and undermining. The MLA has also sought an examination of the hydrological relationship between Chattamakhana Dam and the Lower Suktel Dam. The letter states that Chattamakhana Dam is located around 18 km downstream of Lower Suktel Dam, whose spillway has a design discharge of about 7,035 cumec. It also points to an intervening catchment of approximately 111 sq km that could contribute additional runoff. Singh Deo has asked the inquiry to determine whether the 2,760-cumec design flood for Chattamakhana was correctly assessed and whether it was reviewed after the commissioning of Lower Suktel Dam. The MLA has sought an independent technical inquiry involving the State Dam Safety Organisation and external experts. He has asked for an examination of the sanctioned and constructed parameters, the contractor's justification for the design changes and the records of the authorities that reviewed and approved the final design. He has also sought an investigation into the causes of the damaged cut-off wall and downstream embankments, the present stability of the structure and the possibility of progressive or complete failure. Singh Deo further called for responsibility to be fixed on the contractor and officials involved in the design review and approval if any deficiencies are established. He sought rectification of the structure at the contractor's cost where non-compliance is found, along with an assessment of the quality of materials, workmanship and supervision. The MLA has urged the government to take immediate safety and risk-mitigation measures, including restrictions on impoundment or operation if necessary and downstream warning arrangements. He has also requested that the inquiry report, including the recorded design justifications, approval notes and recommended corrective measures, be placed in the public domain.

articles.title: GeM crosses Rs 20 lakh crore procurement milestone as platform completes 10 years
articles.description: New Delhi, Aug 7 (IANS) The Government e-Marketplace (GeM), the Centre's online public procurement platform, will complete a decade of operations on August 9, marking ten years of efforts to digitise government purchasing and improve transparency in procurement, it was announced on Friday. Over the past decade, the platform has facilitated cumulative transactions worth more than Rs 20 lakh crore through over 3.78 crore orders, the Ministry of Commerce & Industry said. Since its launch in 2016, GeM has witnessed rapid growth in procurement volumes. The platform's annual Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) increased from Rs 422 crore in FY17 to more than Rs 5 lakh crore in each of FY25 and FY26. In the first four months of FY27 alone, GeM recorded a GMV of Rs 1.48 lakh crore. Notably, while the platform took more than eight years to reach its first Rs 10 lakh crore in cumulative GMV, it added the next Rs 10 lakh crore in less than two years, as per its regulatory filing. The marketplace has also seen a sharp rise in participation. The number of profile-completed sellers on the platform has grown from 3,339 at inception to 25.45 lakh, while the number of primary buyer organisations has expanded from 1,707 to 1.37 lakh. Registrations by Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) have increased significantly from 2,424 to 12.25 lakh over the same period. GeM said the platform has played a key role in promoting inclusive procurement. MSEs have fulfilled orders worth more than Rs 9.07 lakh crore, accounting for 45.6 per cent of the cumulative GMV generated on the portal. Women-led MSEs have completed over 50 lakh orders valued at more than Rs 99,147 crore, while 42,242 startups have secured government orders worth over Rs 65,633 crore through the marketplace. According to an IIT Delhi study covering the period from FY24 to FY26, GeM generated a monetised benefit of Rs 86,571.69 crore through improvements in pricing and procurement processes, resulting in a net social saving of Rs 1.76 lakh crore. The study also found that GeM offered lower prices than other e-marketplaces for 74.3 per cent of 101 products examined, translating into a spend-weighted saving of 13.6 per cent. --IANS pk

articles.title: GeM crosses Rs 20 lakh crore procurement milestone
articles.description: India's GeM portal has facilitated over twenty lakh crore rupees in procurement. This platform has seen millions of sellers and enterprises participate actively. articles.title: FCIK seeks stronger industry support in revised Industrial Policy
articles.description: The Federation of Chambers of Industries Kashmir (FCIK) on Thursday submitted a comprehensive Executive Policy Memorandum to the Government, presenting industry’s perspective on the proposed Institutional Framework for Effective Ease of Doing Business and the Revised Industrial Policy in a consolidated form. The 17-page Memorandum was submitted by an FCIK delegation led by Shahid Kamili to the Drafting Committee constituted by the Government under the chairmanship of Shailender Kumar, Financial Commissioner (Additional Chief Secretary), Finance Department, during the second and final round of stakeholder consultations held at the TRC Conference Hall, Srinagar. The meeting was attended by the other two members of the Drafting Committee, Vikramjeet Singh, Commissioner/Secretary, Industries & Commerce Department, and Amitava Chatterjee, Managing Director & CEO, J&K Bank. Also present were Anil Banka, Director, Industries & Commerce, Kashmir, Zahoor Ahmad Magrey and Rayees Ahmad Bhat, Joint Directors, Industries & Commerce, General Managers of District Industries Centres across Kashmir, senior officers of the Industries & Commerce Department and its Public Sector Undertakings, besides representatives of various trade and business organisations. The Executive Policy Memorandum consolidates the principal concerns and recommendations contained in FCIK’s earlier comprehensive submissions, together with several additional policy suggestions emerging from extensive consultations with industrial associations and stakeholders. It seeks to provide a practical policy blueprint for the Revised Industrial Policy by outlining industry’s perspective on the institutional framework for effective Ease of Doing Business and the policy provisions required to create a competitive, investment-friendly and employment-oriented industrial ecosystem in Jammu & Kashmir. During the deliberations, the FCIK delegation comprehensively articulated the concerns and aspirations of the industrial sector and actively participated in detailed discussions with the Drafting Committee on a wide range of policy issues affecting the industrial and MSME ecosystem of the Union Territory. Among its principal recommendations, FCIK has proposed a statutory and technology-driven Ease of Doing Business framework, restoration and strengthening of District Industries Centres, a single integrated Industrial Policy applicable to existing, revived, expanding and new industrial units, a comprehensive revival and rehabilitation package for stressed MSMEs, broad parity with the incentive architecture of the New Central Sector Scheme, and long-term policy stability to restore investor confidence. The Memorandum also advocates major reforms in public procurement by reviving SICOP as the nodal procurement and marketing agency on the lines of GeM portal, introducing purchase preference for local manufacturing enterprises, strengthening local participation on the GeM Portal, ensuring MSME-friendly e-tendering, segregating supply contracts from works contracts, and eliminating restrictive tender conditions that impede participation of local manufacturers. Recognising the importance of industrial competitiveness, FCIK has further recommended strengthening industrial infrastructure, improving institutional credit flow, rationalising statutory charges, ensuring timely payments to MSMEs, promoting employment-linked and green industrialisation, and introducing dedicated sector-specific policies for wood-based, mineral-based, agro and horticulture processing, food processing, poultry, printing and packaging, handicrafts and other resource-based industries. It has also proposed strengthening key institutions such as SIDCO, SICOP, District Industries Centres and the MSME Facilitation Council, besides establishing robust monitoring and grievance redressal mechanisms to ensure effective implementation of the revised policy. The chairman of the committee Shailender Kumar appreciated the comprehensive and well-structured submissions made by FCIK and engaged in detailed deliberations on several of the key policy issues raised in the Memorandum. A meaningful exchange of views took place on matters relating to Ease of Doing Business, revival of existing industries, public procurement reforms, institutional strengthening, fiscal support and credit flow to MSMEs. The Committee acknowledged the valuable contribution of stakeholders to the policy formulation process and assured the participants that all suggestions received from industry and other stakeholders would be examined objectively while finalising the Revised Industrial Policy. The Chairman informed the meeting that the Drafting Committee would endeavour to complete the exercise and place the draft policy before the Government at the earliest for its consideration and approval.
